database_summary: This is a Sakila-like DVD rental schema implemented in SQLite. It models films, people (actors, staff, customers), physical inventory at stores, rentals and payments, and geographic/address hierarchy (country -> city -> address). Tables include descriptive (dimension-like) tables (actor, language, category, country, city, address, store, staff), entity tables (film, customer, inventory), and event/history tables (rental, payment, film_actor, film_category). Row counts indicate a small/medium OLTP dataset (films ~1000, customers ~599, rentals/payments ~16k).

accepted.name: film_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  title,
  description,
  release_year,
  language_id,
  original_language_id,
  rental_duration,
  rental_rate,
  length,
  replacement_cost,
  rating,
  special_features,
  last_update
FROM film
accepted.description: Normalized projection of the film table with key descriptive attributes and numeric measures canonicalized. Use this as the base film dimension for joins, aggregations, or filters. | Use for: Per-film aggregations (rentals/payments/inventory counts), film listings and filters by language/rating/release_year, joins to category/actor

accepted.name: film_by_language_category
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.film_id,
  f.title,
  f.release_year,
  f.language_id,
  l.name AS name,
  fc.category_id,
  c.name AS category_name,
  f.rental_rate,
  f.length,
  f.rating
FROM film f
LEFT JOIN language l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
LEFT JOIN film_category fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
LEFT JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
accepted.description: Denormalized view of films joined to their language(s) and category assignment(s). Each row is one film-category combination with language names for easy groupings and filters. | Use for: Counts or averages of films by category or language, filters like films in a category or language, cross tabs of rating by category

accepted.name: inventory_per_film_store
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  film_id,
  store_id,
  COUNT(*) AS inventory_count
FROM inventory
GROUP BY film_id, store_id
accepted.description: Aggregated counts of inventory copies per film and per store. Useful for inventory availability, joining to rentals to compute utilization, or ranking films by stock. | Use for: Which films have the most/fewest copies per store, inventory joins to rentals to compute utilization or availability

accepted.name: rental_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  rental_id,
  rental_date,
  inventory_id,
  customer_id,
  return_date,
  staff_id,
  last_update
FROM rental
accepted.description: Clean projection of rental events exposing key timestamps and references. Use as the canonical rental event table for time-based analyses, joins to inventory/customer/staff, or windowing. | Use for: Rental activity over time, average rental duration, late returns, per-customer or per-staff rental counts

accepted.name: payments_per_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  SUM(amount) AS payment_total
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id
accepted.description: Aggregated payment totals and counts per customer. Useful for lifetime value, recent revenue by customer, and joining to customer demographics. | Use for: Top customers by revenue, average payment size per customer, segmentation by total spend

accepted.name: customer_address_city_country
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  cu.customer_id,
  cu.store_id,
  cu.first_name,
  cu.last_name,
  cu.email,
  cu.address_id,
  a.address,
  a.address2,
  a.district,
  a.city_id,
  ci.city AS city,
  ci.country_id,
  co.country AS country,
  a.postal_code,
  a.phone,
  cu.active,
  cu.create_date,
  cu.last_update
FROM customer cu
LEFT JOIN address a ON cu.address_id = a.address_id
LEFT JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id
LEFT JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id
accepted.description: Denormalized customer contact info joined through address -> city -> country. One row per customer with their address and geographic names. | Use for: Customer geographic distributions, mailing lists, regional revenue by joining to payments, filtering active customers by country/city

accepted.name: film_actor_roster
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.film_id,
  fa.actor_id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  fa.last_update
FROM film_actor fa
LEFT JOIN actor a ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
accepted.description: One row per film-actor assignment with actor names included. Useful for credit listings, actor film counts, or filtering films by actor. | Use for: Find all films for a given actor, count films per actor, build actor filmographies

accepted.name: customer_payment_ranks
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.payment_id,
  p.customer_id,
  p.amount,
  p.payment_date,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.customer_id ORDER BY p.payment_date DESC, p.payment_id DESC) AS payment_rank,
  SUM(p.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY p.customer_id ORDER BY p.payment_date DESC, p.payment_id DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total
FROM payment p
accepted.description: Per-customer payments ranked by payment_date with cumulative payment running total. Exposes payment rank and running_total so callers can select recent N or compute lifetime contributions up to a rank. | Use for: Latest N payments per customer, cumulative spend over time per customer, recent activity detection

accepted.name: customer_ltv_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  COALESCE(p.payment_count,0) AS payment_count,
  COALESCE(p.payment_total,0.0) AS payment_total,
  COALESCE(r.rental_count,0) AS rental_count,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(p.payment_count,0) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE COALESCE(p.payment_total,0.0) / p.payment_count END AS avg_payment
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS payment_count, SUM(amount) AS payment_total
  FROM payment
  GROUP BY customer_id
) p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS rental_count
  FROM rental
  GROUP BY customer_id
) r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
accepted.description: Customer lifetime summary combining payments and rentals: total payments, payment count, total rentals, and average payment amount. Use for customer segmentation and LTV calculations. | Use for: Customer lifetime value, segmentation by total spend and activity, average payment behaviour
